title: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer
body:
Read the chapter → [Psalms 109](/bible/psalms/109)

[Psalm 109](/bible/psalms/109) is a prayer of David against the enemies, the same kind of prayer seen in [Luke 18](/bible/luke/18) where we always pray for the destruction of our enemies. David gives himself unto prayer, letting God fight his battles against the nations that reward evil for good, and asks that the reward of the adversaries come from the Lord.

**[Psalms 109:1-5](/bible/psalms/109#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/109#v1)</sup> Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise;
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/109#v2)</sup> For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me: they have spoken against me with a lying tongue.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/109#v3)</sup> They compassed me about also with words of hatred; and fought against me without a cause.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/109#v4)</sup> For my love they are my adversaries: but I give myself unto prayer.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/109#v5)</sup> And they have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love.

- Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise, for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are open against me, and they have spoken against me with a lying tongue. The people speaking against us are the nations.
- They compassed me about also with words of hatred and fought against me without a cause. For my love they are my adversaries, but I give myself unto prayer. We have to give ourselves unto prayer and let God fight our battles, for it is not by our might.
  - **[Lamentations 3:46](/bible/lamentations/3#v46)**
    > <sup>[46](/bible/lamentations/3#v46)</sup> All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.

    All our enemies have opened their mouths against us, and these enemies are the nations.
  - **[Luke 18](/bible/luke/18)**  *1 And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint; 2 Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man: 3 And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary. 4 And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; 5 Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me. 6 And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith. 7 And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them? 8 I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth? 9 And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others: 10 Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican. 11 The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. 12 I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. 13 And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. 14 I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted. 15 And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them. 16 But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God. 17 Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein. 18 And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? 19 And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God. 20 Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother. 21 And he said, All these have I kept from my youth up. 22 Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me. 23 And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich. 24 And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God! 25 For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. 26 And they that heard it said, Who then can be saved? 27 And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God. 28 Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee. 29 And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God’s sake, 30 Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting. 31 Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished. 32 For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on: 33 And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again. 34 And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken. 35 And it came to pass, that as he was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging: 36 And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant. 37 And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by. 38 And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me. 39 And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me. 40 And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him, 41 Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight. 42 And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee. 43 And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.*  This is the same pattern of always praying to God for the destruction of our enemies.

**[Psalms 109:6-15](/bible/psalms/109#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/psalms/109#v6)</sup> Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/109#v7)</sup> When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/109#v8)</sup> Let his days be few; and let another take his office.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/109#v9)</sup> Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/109#v10)</sup> Let his children be continually vagabonds, and beg: let them seek their bread also out of their desolate places.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/psalms/109#v11)</sup> Let the extortioner catch all that he hath; and let the strangers spoil his labour.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/psalms/109#v12)</sup> Let there be none to extend mercy unto him: neither let there be any to favour his fatherless children.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/psalms/109#v13)</sup> Let his posterity be cut off; and in the generation following let their name be blotted out.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/psalms/109#v14)</sup> Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered with the Lord; and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/psalms/109#v15)</sup> Let them be before the Lord continually, that he may cut off the memory of them from the earth.

- Set thou a wicked man over him and let Satan stand at his right hand; when he shall be judged let him be condemned, and let his prayer become sin. Let his days be few and let another take his office, his rulership.
- Let his children be fatherless and his wife a widow; let his children be continually vagabonds, meaning bums, and beg, seeking their bread out of their desolate places, walking around like bums begging for crumbs.
- Let the extortioner catch all that he hath and let the strangers spoil his labor; let there be none to extend mercy unto him nor to favor his fatherless children. Let his posterity, his future generations, be cut off and their name blotted out.
- Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered with the Lord and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out; let them be before the Lord continually, that He may cut off the memory of them from the earth, that they may be destroyed.

**[Psalms 109:16-20](/bible/psalms/109#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/psalms/109#v16)</sup> Because that he remembered not to shew mercy, but persecuted the poor and needy man, that he might even slay the broken in heart.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/psalms/109#v17)</sup> As he loved cursing, so let it come unto him: as he delighted not in blessing, so let it be far from him.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/psalms/109#v18)</sup> As he clothed himself with cursing like as with his garment, so let it come into his bowels like water, and like oil into his bones.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/psalms/109#v19)</sup> Let it be unto him as the garment which covereth him, and for a girdle wherewith he is girded continually.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/psalms/109#v20)</sup> Let this be the reward of mine adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul.

- Because he remembered not to show mercy but persecuted the poor and needy man, that he might even slay the broken in heart. The enemies showed us no mercy in captivity and continued to destroy us even when our iniquity came to an end.
- As he loved cursing, so let it come unto him; as he delighted not in blessing, so let it be far from him. This is the nations doing their own will against the Israelites, afflicting the poor.
- Let this be the reward of my adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord fights for us against our enemies to save us.
  - **[Isaiah 14:32](/bible/isaiah/14#v32)**
    > <sup>[32](/bible/isaiah/14#v32)</sup> What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.

    What shall one answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of His people, the Israelites, shall trust in it.
  - **[Psalms 40:8](/bible/psalms/40#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/40#v8)</sup> I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.

    I delight to do thy will, O my God; if you are doing God's will you will do the laws of God.
  - **[Tobit 4:5](/bible/tobit/4#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/tobit/4#v5)</sup> My son, be mindful of the Lord our God all thy days, and let not thy will be set to sin, or to transgress his commandments: do uprightly all thy life long, and follow not the ways of unrighteousness.

    Be mindful of the Lord all your days and let not your will be set to sin or transgress His commandments; if you are not doing God's will you are doing your own will, as the nations do.
  - **[Deuteronomy 20:4](/bible/deuteronomy/20#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/20#v4)</sup> For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.

    The Lord your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies to save you.
  - **[Zechariah 14:3](/bible/zechariah/14#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/zechariah/14#v3)</sup> Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.

    The Lord shall go forth and fight against those nations, the enemies He fights against.

**[Psalms 109:21-25](/bible/psalms/109#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/psalms/109#v21)</sup> But do thou for me, O God the Lord, for thy name’s sake: because thy mercy is good, deliver thou me.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/psalms/109#v22)</sup> For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/psalms/109#v23)</sup> I am gone like the shadow when it declineth: I am tossed up and down as the locust.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/psalms/109#v24)</sup> My knees are weak through fasting; and my flesh faileth of fatness.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/psalms/109#v25)</sup> I became also a reproach unto them: when they looked upon me they shaked their heads.

- But do thou for me, O God the Lord, for thy name's sake; because thy mercy is good, deliver thou me. For I am poor and needy and my heart is wounded within me; I am gone like the shadow when it declineth and am tossed up and down as the locust.
- My knees are weak through fasting and my flesh faileth of fatness, meaning I am skinny now. I have become also a reproach unto the adversaries; when they look upon me they shake their heads.

**[Psalms 109:26-31](/bible/psalms/109#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/psalms/109#v26)</sup> Help me, O Lord my God: O save me according to thy mercy:
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/psalms/109#v27)</sup> That they may know that this is thy hand; that thou, Lord, hast done it.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/psalms/109#v28)</sup> Let them curse, but bless thou: when they arise, let them be ashamed; but let thy servant rejoice.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/psalms/109#v29)</sup> Let mine adversaries be clothed with shame, and let them cover themselves with their own confusion, as with a mantle.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/psalms/109#v30)</sup> I will greatly praise the Lord with my mouth; yea, I will praise him among the multitude.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/psalms/109#v31)</sup> For he shall stand at the right hand of the poor, to save him from those that condemn his soul.

- Help me, O Lord my God; O save me according to thy mercy, that they, the adversaries, may know that this is thy hand, that thou, Lord, hast done it. The destruction of the nations will be by the Lord's Spirit.
- Let them curse, but bless thou; when they arise let them be ashamed, but let thy servant rejoice. Let the adversaries be clothed with shame and cover themselves with their own confusion. The nations meant evil against us, but God means it for good.
- I will greatly praise the Lord with my mouth and praise Him among the multitude, for He shall stand at the right hand of the poor, the Israelites, to save him from those that condemn his soul. He saves the poor by His commandments; keeping God's commandments and enduring in this truth is how we will be saved.
  - **[Zechariah 4:6](/bible/zechariah/4#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/zechariah/4#v6)</sup> Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.

    Not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit, saith the Lord of hosts; these things, the destroying of the nations, will be by the Lord's Spirit.
  - **[Genesis 50:20](/bible/genesis/50#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/genesis/50#v20)</sup> But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

    The nations thought evil against us, but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass as it is this day to save much people alive.
